# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 1B.8 evidence note

Overall read: **mildly favorable, low confidence**. The 2024 record shows repeated public de-escalation language and institutional deterrence framing, but I found little direct evidence of crisis-channel management beyond speeches and official nuclear-stability messaging.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | PM urges India to engage in dialogue for resolution of J&K dispute | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | In his UNGA address, Sharif urged India to enter dialogue for a peaceful resolution of Kashmir. That is the clearest 2024 de-escalatory statement and supports preserved channels for reducing accidental war. | 1B.8; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |
| Favorable | Chill of a new Cold War is in the air, Pakistan leader tells UN Assembly | UN Geneva | 2024-09-27 | https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98067/chill-new-cold-war-air-pakistan-leader-tells-un-assembly | The UN Geneva summary of Sharif’s UNGA remarks emphasizes diplomacy, terrorism, and a dangerous international environment. This is consistent with a public attempt to lower tension and preserve diplomatic channels. | 1B.8; also 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| Favorable | PM voices satisfaction over Pakistan Army’s operational preparedness | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-05 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/05-09-2024/pm-expresses-satisfaction-over-pak-armys-operational-preparedness | Sharif said preparedness helps preserve “the delicate balance of power essential for peace in nuclearized South Asia” and framed deterrence as a cost only “in the event of aggression.” This is stabilizing rhetoric, not escalation. | 1B.8; also 1B.5, 1B.7 |
| Mixed | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | The same UNGA speech also contained hard-edged language about India’s military expansion and a “limited war under the nuclear overhanging,” which is confrontational even though it stops short of a direct nuclear threat. | 1B.8; also 1B.2, 1B.5 |
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif publicly described Pakistan’s nuclear program as peaceful, defensive, and non-aggressive. That is consistent with clear, restraint-oriented signaling in a tense strategic environment. | 1B.8; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |

## Search gap

- I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence of backchannel crisis management, hotline use, military-to-military deconfliction, or a specific acute war scare where Sharif personally stepped in to cool tensions.
- I also did **not** find credible evidence that he worsened an acute crisis through unclear signaling.
- So the best-supported conclusion is that Sharif’s 2024 behavior was **mostly de-escalatory in public messaging**, but the record does not strongly show hands-on crisis management.
